title: Presente perfecto con ever / never (experiencias)
short: Have you ever been to Canada? I've never tried it. Para hablar de lo que has hecho (o no) en tu vida.

story.title: ¿Alguna vez…?
story.text: Para preguntar por experiencias de toda la vida usamos ==Have you ever…?== Ever significa «alguna vez» y va justo antes del participio.

examples.t: Have you ever been to Canada?
Has your son ever flown alone?
examples.es: ¿Ha volado tu hijo solo alguna vez?

story.title: Preguntar y responder
story.text: La respuesta corta repite ==have / has==. Con never la frase ya es negativa.

story.title: never = nunca (una sola negación)
story.text: Never ya es negativo. Por eso va con ==have==, no con haven't. En inglés no se dice «no nunca».

examples.t: I've never been on a cruise.
My husband has never eaten snails.
examples.es: Mi marido nunca ha comido caracoles.

story.title: been to y gone to
story.text: ==been to== = has ido y has vuelto (experiencia). ==gone to== = se ha ido y todavía está allí.

examples.es: He estado en Toronto (y ya volví).
Hugo se ha ido a Toronto (está allí).

story.title: ¿Cuántas veces?
story.text: Al final de la frase: ==once== (una vez), ==twice== (dos veces), ==three times==, ==many times==.

examples.es: He estado en Londres dos veces.

examples.t: We've seen that film three times.
examples.es: Hemos visto esa película tres veces.

story.title: Así en español, así en inglés
story.text: «¿Has estado alguna vez…?» funciona casi igual. Pero en cuanto das detalles (cuándo, con quién), el inglés pasa a ==pasado simple==.

examples.t: Have you ever been to Paris? — Yes, I have.
When did you go? — I went in 2018.

story.title: Errores típicos
story.text:
❌ I haven't never been. ✅ I've ==never== been.
❌ Did you ever go to Rome? (suena americano) ✅ ==Have== you ever ==been== to Rome?
❌ I've been in Canada in 2015. ✅ I ==went== to Canada in 2015.

story.title: Truco para charlar
story.text: Abre con ==Have you ever…?== y sigue con preguntas en pasado: ==When did you go? What was it like?== Así se charla en inglés.

compare.es: En español decimos «¿Has estado alguna vez en Roma?» y «Nunca he estado», y podemos usar doble negación: «No he estado nunca».
compare.target: En inglés se usa igual el present perfect con ever (en preguntas) y never (una sola negación: I've never been, nunca I haven't never). En británico se prefiere Have you ever…? a Did you ever…? Al dar detalles concretos, se cambia a pasado simple: I went in 2018.

errors.wrong: I haven't never been to Canada.
errors.why: En inglés solo hay una negación: never ya niega, así que va con have.

errors.wrong: Did you ever go to Scotland?
errors.right: Have you ever been to Scotland?
errors.why: En inglés británico, para experiencias de toda la vida se usa Have you ever…?
Con una fecha pasada se usa pasado simple.

errors.wrong: Have you ever been in London?
errors.right: Have you ever been to London?
errors.why: Para viajes, la experiencia es been to + lugar.
Ever va en preguntas, no en frases afirmativas.

errors.wrong: Have you ever been to Rome? — Yes, I went.
errors.right: Have you ever been to Rome? — Yes, I have.
errors.why: La respuesta corta repite el auxiliar: Yes, I have.

exercises.q: Have you ___ been to Canada?
exercises.why: En preguntas sobre experiencias: Have you ever…?

exercises.q: I've ___ eaten snails. I don't want to try them!
exercises.why: Never = nunca, con el verbo en afirmativa.

exercises.q: Have you ever tried maple syrup? — Yes, I ___.
exercises.why: La respuesta corta repite el auxiliar: Yes, I have.

exercises.q: Has your son ever lived abroad? — No, he ___.
exercises.why: Pregunta con has → respuesta con hasn't.

exercises.q: My friend isn't here. She's ___ to the market.
exercises.why: Ha ido y sigue allí: gone to.

exercises.q: I've ___ to Toronto. It was wonderful.
exercises.why: Fuiste y ya has vuelto: been to.

exercises.q: We've visited Lisbon ___. Once in 2010 and once last year.
exercises.why: Dos veces = twice.

exercises.q: Have you ___ seen a whale?
exercises.why: Alguna vez, en pregunta: ever.

exercises.q: My husband has ___ been on a plane.
exercises.es: Mi marido nunca ha subido a un avión.
exercises.why: Nunca = never, entre has y el participio.

exercises.q: I've been to London ___. Only one time.
exercises.es: He estado en Londres una vez.
exercises.why: Una vez = once.

exercises.q: ___ she ever travelled alone?
exercises.why: Con she: Has she ever…?

exercises.q: Have they ever ___ in a castle?
exercises.es: ¿Han dormido alguna vez en un castillo?
exercises.why: Sleep → slept → slept.

exercises.q: I've never ___ so much snow!
exercises.why: Participio de see: seen.

exercises.q: Have you ever ___ in a lake?
exercises.why: Swim → swam → swum.

exercises.q: I've never ___ on the left.
exercises.why: Drive → drove → driven.

exercises.q: Has she ever ___ a horse?
exercises.why: Ride → rode → ridden.

exercises.q: You have been to Scotland.
answer: Have you ever been to Scotland?
exercises.why: Have + you + ever + participio.

exercises.q: Your daughter has tried sushi.
answer: Has your daughter ever tried sushi?
exercises.why: Has + sujeto + ever + participio.

exercises.q: I haven't been on a cruise.
answer: I've never been on a cruise.
I have never been on a cruise.
exercises.why: haven't → have never. Una sola negación.

exercises.q: He hasn't seen the sea.
answer: He has never seen the sea.
exercises.why: hasn't → has never.

exercises.q: I haven't never been to America.
exercises.why: Con never el verbo va en afirmativa: I have never been.

exercises.q: Have you ever been in Toronto?
exercises.why: Para la experiencia de un viaje: been to + lugar.

exercises.q: I have ever eaten frogs' legs.
exercises.why: Ever va en preguntas. En afirmativa, never (nunca) o nada.

exercises.q: Have you ever went to Ireland?
exercises.why: Detrás de have va el participio: been.

exercises.q: Has he ever eaten paella? — Yes, he did.
exercises.why: Pregunta con has → respuesta Yes, he has.

exercises.answer: Have you ever been to Canada
exercises.why: Have + you + ever + been to + lugar.

exercises.es: Nunca he viajado en primera clase
exercises.answer: I have never travelled first class
exercises.why: Never va entre have y el participio.

exercises.es: Mi hijo ha estado en Londres muchas veces
exercises.answer: My son has been to London many times
exercises.why: Las veces van al final: many times.

exercises.q: ¿Has probado alguna vez la comida india?
answer: Have you ever tried Indian food?
exercises.why: Probar comida = try: Have you ever tried…?

exercises.q: Nunca he estado en Escocia.
answer: I have never been to Scotland.
exercises.why: Una sola negación: I've never been to…

exercises.q: Have you ever lost your luggage?
exercises.why: Have you ever lost = ¿has perdido alguna vez?

exercises.context: Quieres saber si tu nueva amiga canadiense ha estado en España.
options: Have you ever been to Spain?
Did you ever be in Spain?
Have you never been to Spain?
exercises.answer: Have you ever been to Spain?
exercises.why: Pregunta de experiencia: Have you ever been to…?

exercises.context: Te preguntan si has hecho un crucero. Nunca lo has hecho, pero te encantaría.
options: No, never, but I'd love to!
exercises.answer: No, never, but I'd love to!
exercises.why: Respuesta natural: No, never. I'd love to = me encantaría.

exercises.context: Tu amiga dice «I've been to Toronto!». Quieres saber cuándo fue.
exercises.why: Con when preguntamos por un momento concreto: pasado simple.
Palabras para contar experiencias.

pairs: Have you ever been to Rome?
exercises.why: Pregunta y respuesta: have/has con have/has; did con pasado.
